plan.activation_condition: Observable when the admissible experiment spans small and moderate temperature differences so that |T2 - T1| is not negligible compared with the scale over which contact conductance changes, while both bodies remain well mixed and the contact remains passive.
plan.train_hidden_contrast: In training, varying the initial temperature gap already changes the early-time slope of T1 beyond simple proportional scaling; in holdout with even larger but still physically admissible gaps, the same contrast extends as stronger initial relaxation curvature toward the same conserved mean.
plan.continuation_path: Recover the parent law in the limit of temperature-independent conductance, equivalently when the conductance-modulation scale is very large relative to |T2 - T1| over all observed trajectories.
plan.gap_statement: The model treats thermal contact conductance as constant even when the temperature drop across the interface changes substantially, omitting a common source of nonlinear heat-transfer strength.
plan.scientific_mechanism: Temperature-difference-dependent effective thermal contact conductance at the interface, arising from realistic contact physics or transfer coefficients that vary with contact temperature conditions.
plan.rationale: A natural next refinement is to relax the idealization of constant contact conductance rather than add a new process. The parent target mapping uses a single fixed gain from temperature difference to dT1_dt, so every trajectory differs only by the current value of T2 - T1. Holding heat capacities fixed and preserving isolation, if one compares admissible runs with different initial temperature separations, the parent predicts the same normalized slope dT1_dt/(T2 - T1) at all times. In contrast, with temperature-dependent conductance, that normalized slope changes with |T2 - T1|: large separations produce stronger initial heat exchange and faster early curvature of T1(t), while small separations revert toward the parent linear behavior. This changes the scored target mapping directly because dT1_dt at a given observed (T1,T2) depends nonlinearly on the separation, not merely through auxiliary hidden dynamics. The effect is scientifically admissible whenever the interface transfer coefficient varies appreciably across the temperature-drop range sampled; if the sampled range is too narrow, the refinement may be hard to distinguish and the parent becomes an adequate approximation.

Vary the instantaneous contrast |T2-T1| along the observed relaxation while holding the same state definitions, energy-conserving two-body setting, and existing mean-temperature/body-1 modifiers fixed. Then compare early times with large |T2-T1| to late times when |T2-T1| is small relative to conductance_deltaT_scale. The child predicts that dT1/dt falls off more steeply near equilibrium than the parent, producing extra curvature in the target mapping and a slower final temperature approach, yet it remains consistent with positive entropy production and correct heat-flow direction because the flux still has the sign of T2-T1. This is a change to the scored target mapping itself, not merely to an auxiliary trajectory, since dT1/dt at the same observed T1,T2 is altered near equilibrium. No new state or input is needed because the omitted effect is a constitutive-shape refinement of an already modeled process, not a missing hidden reservoir. A single refit of the parent's existing amplitudes and scales cannot generally reproduce both the preserved large-contrast behavior and the sharper low-contrast suppression across admissible trajectories, because changing contact_conductance rescales all contrasts and changing conductance_deltaT_scale shifts one onset scale but does not supply an independent near-zero curvature shape.

response_change.parent_relation: The interfacial heat flux is an odd, effectively single-regime function of temperature difference: tanh(Abs(T2 - T1)/conductance_deltaT_scale)*(T2 - T1), so after accounting for the mean-temperature and body-1 factors the target depends on |T2-T1| through one fixed saturation shape.
response_change.child_relation: Replace the near-equilibrium conductance transition with a stronger low-contrast suppression consistent with diffusive constriction/microcontact effects, so the target becomes more strongly curved in |T2-T1| near equilibrium while recovering the parent large-contrast behavior at higher |T2-T1|.
response_change.observable_effect: Holding the same initial temperatures and parameters except for the new shape refinement, late-time relaxation near T1≈T2 is slower than the parent predicts, while early-time large-contrast cooling remains close to the parent law.

contract.activation_condition: Observable when |T2-T1| becomes small compared with conductance_deltaT_scale during the trajectory; the refinement is most visible in the late-stage approach to equilibrium, while for |T2-T1| much larger than conductance_deltaT_scale both models nearly coincide.
contract.train_hidden_contrast: In training, the mechanism already affects segments of trajectories that pass from large contrast into near-equilibrium; in holdout it extends the same contrast by changing how sharply the target bends downward as |T2-T1|/conductance_deltaT_scale falls below order unity.
contract.continuation_path: Recover the parent law in the limit where the refined near-equilibrium suppression exponent/shape parameter takes its parent value, or equivalently where the added curvature correction tends to zero so the original tanh-based transition is restored.
contract.scientific_mechanism: Real thermal contact often shows a sharper-than-tanh collapse of effective conductance near zero temperature contrast because only a subset of microcontacts or transport channels remain effective close to equilibrium; this changes the low-contrast constitutive shape without introducing a new energy store.
contract.difficulty_rationale: This is harder than a coefficient-only correction because the target now depends on T1 and T2 through a changed nonlinear contrast-shape, not just a rescaled amplitude or shifted single threshold. The squared activation preserves the large-contrast limit while independently altering near-zero curvature, which a one-scale tanh parent cannot emulate with one shared parameter set.
contract.assumption_before: The temperature-difference-dependent conductance reduction has a fixed tanh crossover shape with one universal low-contrast scaling.
contract.assumption_after: The near-equilibrium contact activation is more strongly suppressed than tanh predicts, consistent with microcontact/channel deactivation, while the same large-contrast conductance limit is retained.
contract.before_fragment: contact_conductance*(1 + mean_temperature_conductance_coeff*((T1 + T2)/2 - conductance_reference_temperature))*(1 + body1_contact_temperature_coeff*(T1 - heat_capacity_1_reference_temperature))*tanh(Abs(T2 - T1)/conductance_deltaT_scale)*(T2 - T1)/(heat_capacity_1*(1 + heat_capacity_1_temperature_coeff*(T1 - heat_capacity_1_reference_temperature)))
contract.after_fragment: contact_conductance*(1 + mean_temperature_conductance_coeff*((T1 + T2)/2 - conductance_reference_temperature))*(1 + body1_contact_temperature_coeff*(T1 - heat_capacity_1_reference_temperature))*(tanh(Abs(T2 - T1)/conductance_deltaT_scale))**2*(T2 - T1)/(heat_capacity_1*(1 + heat_capacity_1_temperature_coeff*(T1 - heat_capacity_1_reference_temperature)))
contract.parent_reduction: The parent is recovered by replacing the refined suppression factor (tanh(Abs(T2 - T1)/conductance_deltaT_scale))**2 with tanh(Abs(T2 - T1)/conductance_deltaT_scale), i.e. restoring the original single-shape crossover.
contract.observable_signature: Along the same two-body relaxation trajectory, compare segments with large and small |T2-T1|. At large |T2-T1|/conductance_deltaT_scale the child and parent give nearly the same dT1/dt, but once |T2-T1|/conductance_deltaT_scale falls below order unity the child predicts a distinctly smaller |dT1/dt| and a slower final approach to T1=T2. This is a direct change in the scored mapping from observed T1,T2 to dT1/dt, not merely a change in an auxiliary state.
contract.shortcut_blocked: A single parent parameter refit cannot reproduce both regimes across the same admissible trajectories: changing contact_conductance rescales the whole curve, and changing conductance_deltaT_scale shifts the crossover location but still leaves one fixed tanh near-zero curvature. The child preserves the high-contrast asymptote while imposing stronger low-contrast suppression, so one shared parent parameter set cannot match both the early-time and late-time target responses simultaneously.
